topics.name: Blocks Procs and Lambdas
subtopics: Block Syntax do end and Braces

questions.title: Block Doubler With Yield
questions.description:
Write a method `double_each` that takes an array of integers and uses `yield` to emit each doubled value.

Input Format:
A single line of space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line of space-separated doubled integers.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, each integer between -1000 and 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
def double_each(arr)
  i = 0
  while i < arr.size
    yield arr[i] * 2
    i += 1
  end
end

arr = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
result = []
double_each(arr) { |x| result << x }
puts result.join(" ")

questions.title: ForEach Block Printer do-end
questions.description:
Read a line of space-separated names and greet each using a `do...end` block on `each`.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated names.

Output Format:
One line per name in the form `Hello, NAME`.

Constraints:
1 <= number of names <= 50; each name length between 1 and 20.
questions.subtopic: Block Syntax do end and Braces
questions.sampleoutput1:
Hello, Ada
Hello, Bob
Hello, Cy
questions.output2:
Hello, Al
Hello, Bo
Hello, Cy
Hello, Di
questions.sourcecode:
names = gets.chomp.split
names.each do |name|
  puts "Hello, #{name}"
end

questions.title: Greet If Block Given
questions.description:
Define a method `greet(name)` that checks `block_given?`. If a block is supplied, yield the name to it; otherwise print `Hi there`.

Input Format:
Line 1: a name. Line 2: a flag (1 = use block, 0 = no block).

Output Format:
Either `Hi NAME` or `Hi there`.

Constraints:
Name length 1..30; flag is 0 or 1.
questions.sourcecode:
def greet(name)
  if block_given?
    yield name
  else
    puts "Hi there"
  end
end

name = gets.chomp
flag = gets.to_i
if flag == 1
  greet(name) { |n| puts "Hi #{n}" }
else
  greet(name)
end

questions.title: Discount Proc Application
questions.description:
A boutique runs a flash sale. Build a `Proc` that captures the discount percentage, then apply it to each listed price.

Input Format:
Line 1: space-separated float prices. Line 2: integer discount percent (0..100).

Output Format:
One line of space-separated discounted prices (2 decimals).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; 0.0 <= price <= 10000.0; 0 <= pct <= 100.
questions.sourcecode:
prices = gets.split.map(&:to_f)
pct = gets.to_f
discount = Proc.new { |p| p * (1 - pct / 100.0) }
result = prices.map(&discount)
puts result.map { |v| "%.2f" % v }.join(" ")

questions.title: Greeting Lambda Closure
questions.description:
A reception kiosk greets visitors by name N times. Build a `lambda` closure that captures the visitor's name and returns a numbered greeting per call.

Input Format:
Line 1: visitor name. Line 2: integer n.

Output Format:
N lines of `Hello NAME i` where i goes 1..n.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; name length 1..20.
questions.sampleoutput1:
Hello Ada 1
Hello Ada 2
Hello Ada 3
questions.output2:
Hello Zoe 1
Hello Zoe 2
Hello Zoe 3
Hello Zoe 4
questions.sourcecode:
name = gets.chomp
n = gets.to_i
greeter = lambda { |i| "Hello #{name} #{i}" }
(1..n).each do |i|
  puts greeter.call(i)
end

questions.title: Library Late Fee Yield
questions.description:
A library charges a fixed daily late fee per overdue book. Implement `compute_fees(records, rate)` that yields each `(book_id, fee)` pair when a block is given, otherwise accumulates. The caller block prints and totals.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: `book_id days` separated by space. Daily rate is 0.50.

Output Format:
N lines `BOOK_ID FEE` (2 decimals), then a final line with the total fee (2 decimals).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; 0 <= days <= 365.
questions.sourcecode:
def compute_fees(records, rate)
  results = []
  records.each do |(id, days)|
    fee = days * rate
    if block_given?
      yield id, fee
    else
      results << [id, fee]
    end
  end
  results
end

n = gets.to_i
records = []
n.times do
  parts = gets.split
  records << [parts[0], parts[1].to_i]
end
rate = 0.50
total = 0.0
compute_fees(records, rate) do |id, fee|
  puts "#{id} %.2f" % fee
  total += fee
end
puts "%.2f" % total

questions.title: Bank Withdrawal Ampersand Block
questions.description:
An ATM withdrawal method takes a balance, an amount, and an `&block` authorizer. If the block returns true and amount <= balance, deduct and report OK; if amount exceeds balance, report INSUFFICIENT; if the block returns false, report DENIED.

Input Format:
Line 1: float balance. Line 2: float amount. Line 3: PIN string.

Output Format:
Line 1: status (`OK`, `INSUFFICIENT`, or `DENIED`). Line 2: resulting balance (2 decimals).

Constraints:
0.0 <= balance <= 100000.0; 0.0 <= amount <= 100000.0; PIN length 4.
questions.sourcecode:
def withdraw(balance, amount, &block)
  if block.call
    if amount <= balance
      [balance - amount, "OK"]
    else
      [balance, "INSUFFICIENT"]
    end
  else
    [balance, "DENIED"]
  end
end

balance = gets.to_f
amount = gets.to_f
auth_pin = gets.chomp
stored_pin = "1234"
new_bal, msg = withdraw(balance, amount) { auth_pin == stored_pin }
puts msg
puts "%.2f" % new_bal

questions.title: Order Total With Proc Closure
questions.description:
An e-commerce checkout builds a tax applier as a `Proc` closure capturing the tax rate, then sums taxed amounts for each line item.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Line 2: float tax rate (e.g. 0.08). Next n lines: float line amount.

Output Format:
A single line with the total (2 decimals).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; 0.0 <= rate <= 0.5; 0.0 <= amount <= 10000.0.
questions.sourcecode:
def make_taxer(rate)
  Proc.new { |amt| amt * (1 + rate) }
end

n = gets.to_i
rate = gets.to_f
taxer = make_taxer(rate)
total = 0.0
n.times do
  amt = gets.to_f
  total += taxer.call(amt)
end
puts "%.2f" % total

questions.title: Filter Lambda Strict Arity
questions.description:
A sensor log filter keeps readings above a threshold. Use a `lambda` (which strictly checks arity) as the selector.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: integer readings. Last line: integer threshold.

Output Format:
One line of space-separated readings strictly greater than the threshold.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; -10000 <= reading <= 10000.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
nums = []
n.times { nums << gets.to_i }
threshold = gets.to_i
keep = lambda { |x| x > threshold }
result = nums.select(&keep)
puts result.join(" ")

questions.title: Counter Closure With Proc
questions.description:
A turnstile counter is implemented as a closure: `make_counter` returns a `Proc` that captures a local count and increments it on each call.

Input Format:
A single integer n: how many times to call the counter.

Output Format:
One line of n space-separated counter outputs (1, 2, ..., n).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
def make_counter
  count = 0
  Proc.new do
    count += 1
    count
  end
end

counter = make_counter
n = gets.to_i
results = []
n.times { results << counter.call }
puts results.join(" ")

questions.title: Iterator Builder With Ampersand Block
questions.description:
Build a custom iterator `iterate_all(arr, &block)` that walks the array using a `while` loop and invokes the block via `block.call` for each element. Use it to produce squares of the input integers.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line of space-separated squared integers.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; -1000 <= v <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
def iterate_all(arr, &block)
  i = 0
  while i < arr.size
    block.call(arr[i])
    i += 1
  end
  arr
end

raw = gets.split
arr = []
i = 0
while i < raw.size
  arr << raw[i].to_i
  i += 1
end
squared = []
iterate_all(arr) { |x| squared << x * x }
puts squared.join(" ")

questions.title: Recursive Memoizer Via Lambda Closure
questions.description:
Implement a memoized factorial using a recursive `lambda` closure that stores computed results in a captured hash, plus a `->` printer lambda that formats the output.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated integers (each 0..12).

Output Format:
One line of space-separated factorials.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 0 <= v <= 12.
questions.sourcecode:
memo = {}
fact = lambda do |n|
  if n <= 1
    1
  else
    memo[n] ||= n * fact.call(n - 1)
  end
end

nums = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
printer = ->(arr) { puts arr.join(" ") }
printer.call(nums.map { |x| fact.call(x) })
